{"label":"system_slowness","explanation":"Handle time jumped on both queues at 10:00. Payments AHT was 465 s against 285 s forecast, and general AHT was 646 s against 376 s, up about 55-70%. Volumes were close to forecast: today so far is +1.7% on payments and -1.4% on general, and no call reason shows a meaningful surge. Login_issue on general is only +11 calls. Attendance is normal, with 2 sick on each queue against a usual 2.4-2.6. The jump matches the open P2 incident INC-20261021-5862 (opened 09:55): CRM customer search is taking 20-40 seconds, which inflates every call's handle time. This is internal tool slowness, not a customer-facing outage and not a demand change.","plan_name":"CRM slowness bridge: free capacity on both queues, deflect simple enquiries, targeted overtime","rationale":"The problem is a capacity shortfall caused by longer calls on both queues. That rules out moving cross-skilled agents, since neither queue can donate without dropping below 70%. An outage message would also be wrong because customers are not affected by a known issue. The fix time is uncertain, though an index rebuild is often resolved within hours, so the plan front-loads mostly free levers over roughly the next 2.5 hours.
- Delay breaks on both queues by 30 minutes to cover the immediate gap until overtime arrives.
- Cancel non-mandatory coaching to put agents back on phones.
- Turn on callback offers to flatten the queue peaks.
- Deflect status and balance enquiries to chat at Rs 12 per chat, since these calls need CRM lookups and are slow on the phone right now.
- Offer a single 2-hour overtime block per queue from 10:45, when approved agents can arrive. At about 40% acceptance this is roughly Rs 5,760, well inside the Rs 15,000 budget, leaving room for a second block if the incident runs past
